rawText:
For an **existing upper-upscale hotel in the Caribbean or Latin America**, the owner should generally evaluate **conversion-friendly collection brands first**. They preserve more of the property’s identity, usually require fewer prototype changes than traditional flags, and still provide loyalty, distribution and global sales systems.

## Recommended shortlist

| Brand | Best suited to | Key owner consideration |
|---|---|---|
| **Autograph Collection — Marriott** | Distinctive upper-upscale or luxury resorts and landmark urban hotels | Strong Marriott Bonvoy contribution, but typically expects a compelling concept, elevated design and meaningful F&B. Marriott already uses Autograph extensively for Caribbean all-inclusive resorts. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/premium-brands?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Tribute Portfolio — Marriott** | Independent-feeling upper-upscale hotels requiring somewhat greater flexibility | Often a better fit than Autograph when the asset is lifestyle-oriented but not sufficiently differentiated or luxurious. Marriott explicitly supports existing-hotel conversions under the brand. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/premium-brands?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Curio Collection by Hilton** | Upper-upscale/luxury urban, boutique and resort properties | One of the strongest regional candidates, including all-inclusive conversions. Hilton reported that conversions represented nearly 30% of its 2024 CALA signings, and Curio continues expanding across the region. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hilton-wraps-2024-with-record-portfolio-and-pipeline-growth-in-the-caribbean-and-latin-america?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Tapestry Collection by Hilton** | Smaller, less luxurious or more price-sensitive upper-upscale assets | More flexible positioning than Curio, although it may represent a slight downshift if the hotel currently achieves true upper-upscale ADR and service levels. Hilton describes both collections as flexible conversion platforms. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hiltons-curio-and-tapestry-collections-celebrate-200th-hotel-milestones?utm_source=openai)) |
| **MGallery Collection — Accor** | Design-led boutique hotels, historic properties and culturally distinctive resorts | Particularly relevant where Accor has strong local sales infrastructure. Accor identifies MGallery specifically as its upper-upscale collection brand and prioritizes existing-building conversions for its collection brands. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/news-stories/collection-brands-handwritten-emblems-mgallery?utm_source=openai)) |
| **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt** | High-end experiential resorts and iconic independent hotels | Best for assets capable of luxury-level service and storytelling. Its regional relevance is increasing, including the planned 2026 addition of Cayo Levantado Resort in the Dominican Republic. ([newsroom.hyatt.com](https://newsroom.hyatt.com/UnboundAnniversaryGrowth2026?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Vignette Collection — IHG** | High-quality upper-upscale-to-luxury hotels that should retain their existing name and identity | A purpose-built conversion collection offering rapid access to IHG systems. SOUMA Hotel in Peru converted to the brand in 2025, demonstrating regional applicability. ([development.ihg.com](https://development.ihg.com/hotel-brands/vignette-collection?utm_source=openai)) |
| **voco — IHG** | Larger, more standardized upper-upscale hotels where conversion cost and speed are priorities | Less “independent” than a soft collection but intentionally conversion-friendly, with limited brand standards and comparatively lower capital requirements. IHG opened a converted voco in Mexico City in March 2026. ([development.ihg.com](https://development.ihg.com/hotel-brands/voco-hotels?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Registry Collection Hotels — Wyndham** | Luxury and upper-upscale resorts, especially large all-inclusive properties | Particularly credible in Mexico and the Caribbean through Wyndham’s regional relationships with Palladium and other resort operators. ([corporate.wyndhamhotels.com](https://corporate.wyndhamhotels.com/news-regions/latamc/?utm_source=openai)) |

## If the property is all-inclusive

The shortlist should be adjusted around the target customer:

- **Adults-only luxury:** Secrets, Hyatt Zilara, Curio, Autograph Collection or Registry Collection.
- **Family-oriented luxury:** Hyatt Ziva, Dreams, Autograph Collection or Curio.
- **Wellness or intimate luxury:** Zoëtry, Unbound Collection or Vignette Collection.
- **Social/lifestyle adults-only:** Breathless or Hyatt Vivid.
- **Value-oriented all-inclusive:** Wyndham Alltra, Trademark Collection or selected Marriott alternatives.

Hyatt has the deepest dedicated all-inclusive brand architecture in the region, with brands including Impression by Secrets, Hyatt Ziva, Hyatt Zilara, Zoëtry, Secrets, Breathless, Dreams, Hyatt Vivid, Alua, Sunscape and Bahia Principe. ([newsroom.hyatt.com](https://newsroom.hyatt.com/2025-june-17-playahotelsandresortsacquisition?utm_source=openai))

## Traditional flags worth testing

If the hotel does not possess a strong independent story—or if group, corporate and convention demand matters more than individuality—the owner should also test:

- **Renaissance or Marriott Hotels**
- **Hilton or DoubleTree by Hilton**
- **Hyatt Regency**
- **InterContinental or Crowne Plaza**
- **Pullman**
- **Wyndham Grand**

These can deliver clearer customer recognition but generally impose more standardized physical, operating and service requirements than collection brands.

## Practical initial RFP list

For a typical upper-upscale, full-service asset, I would invite proposals from:

1. **Autograph Collection**
2. **Curio Collection**
3. **MGallery**
4. **Vignette Collection**
5. **The Unbound Collection**
6. **voco**
7. **Tribute Portfolio**
8. **Registry Collection**, particularly for a resort or all-inclusive asset

The selection should ultimately be based on a **10-year owner cash-flow comparison**, not simply the strongest consumer brand. Compare:

- Required property-improvement-plan capital
- Franchise versus management structure
- Base, incentive, reservation, marketing and loyalty fees
- Estimated brand-system room contribution
- Displacement of existing direct and wholesale business
- All-inclusive tour-operator connectivity
- Owner termination and performance-test rights
- Key money or renovation support
- Territorial protection
- Ramp-up period and conversion closure requirements
- Ability to retain the hotel’s existing name, management company and F&B concepts

**Bottom line:** For most upper-upscale conversions in the region, **Curio, Autograph, Tribute, MGallery, Vignette and Unbound** constitute the strongest soft-brand comparison set. Add **voco** when minimizing conversion capital is important and **Registry or Hyatt’s Inclusive Collection** when the asset is a large all-inclusive resort.
